attributes.residual: NO CHANGE RETAINED. Baseline re-derived live and unchanged at open and close: real 869, insns 575/576, opcode multiset 5t, fuzzy 95.6052%, frame 592. VERDICT ON THE ASSIGNED HYPOTHESIS: NEGATIVE - there is NO large-aggregate-by-value call in fn_8001267C, on five independent lines of evidence. (1) CALL CENSUS: the target contains EXACTLY FOUR bl instructions - fn_80011DCC @0x360, SetupAnimHeader @0x78c, InitOAnimList @0x820, FatalError @0x8b8 - and ours contains the SAME four callees in the SAME order at 0x360/0x790/0x824/0x8bc. There is no missing call to find. (2) NO INDIRECT CALLS: neither side has bctrl/blrl. (3) THE REGION IS NEVER ADDRESSED: the target references not one byte of r1+8..r1+303. Its ONLY non-memory r1 use in the whole function is the epilogue addi r1,r1,592 - there is no addi rX,r1,N and no mr rX,r1, so the region's address is never even formed, let alone written. A by-value argument area that no instruction stores into cannot be an argument area in use. (4) INSTRUCTION BUDGET: target 575 insns vs ours 576, opcode multiset differing by only +2 li / -1 addi -2 mr. A ~284-byte by-value argument does not compile to zero instructions - MEASURED positive control: passing a 296-byte struct by value emits li r0,37 + mtctr + an 8-byte-per-iteration copy loop and grows the frame to 640. No such copy loop, mtctr, or memcpy call exists anywhere in the target. (5) CALLEE PROTOTYPE AUDIT (Xbox PDB, research/xbox_symbols/functions_by_module.txt): SetupAnimHeader is 41 BYTES of Xbox code and InitOAnimList is 72 BYTES - neither can receive a ~284-byte aggregate; and research/xbox_symbols/xbox_structs.tsv contains no 284- or 296-byte record at all (nearest are WORLDPSYS 312 = the 0x138 stride fn_80011DCC already walks, and PSYS 304). NEW QUANTITATIVE RESULT worth more than the negative: the bottom region is EXACTLY 284 BYTES, not the 296 previously reported, measured by linear calibration rather than inference. A 296-byte by-value parameter places the temps at r1+316; ours with a zero parameter area places them at r1+20; both fit temps_base = 8 + P + 12, i.e. a CONSTANT 12-byte gap sits between the parameter area and the temp region. The target's temps begin at r1+304, so P = 284 exactly. NEW AXIS CLOSED (not covered by the prior law, which tested only outer-block declaration order, alignment and liveness): INNER-BLOCK SCOPE DEPTH. Declaring u8 unused[248] inside the per-match loop's inner block still placed it ABOVE the temps and REGRESSED real 869 -> 879, so scope depth does not move a named local below the temps either. Removing the pad entirely gives our natural frame: 344 bytes, temps at r1+20..305, saved r23-r31 at r1+308, real 875. NEXT WORKER: do NOT hunt a by-value call and do NOT add or reshape a pad - both axes are now closed by measurement. The open question is narrow and named: what sizes an MWCC outgoing-parameter area to 284 bytes while emitting NO argument stores? The surviving candidates, none yet tested, are (a) a call eliminated AFTER frame layout, (b) an inlined callee whose own parameter area merged into this frame while its call was folded away, (c) a per-TU codegen option artifact. A collateral clue for whoever takes it: the target is more temp-frugal than us - it uses 255 temp bytes and 8 callee-saved GPRs (r24-r31) where we use 286 temp bytes and 9 (r23-r31) - so the target's SWAP source form differs from ours in a way that both saves a register and reserves 284 bytes it never uses.
